comments.text:
Hey Amit, firstly, congrats on getting back your classic 350. I know it must have felt great because I went through something similar with my Speed 400 last year. Just 2 months after getting it, I had an accident with another motorcycle on a highway near Hyderabad. The whole front end was gone. It was in Retro Triumph Hyd for one and half month. I could feel what you were going through in the video :)

My bill came out to 60k and I wanted to share few points:

1.) I didn’t have to file an FIR or complaint with the police. I collided with another motorcycle that swerved lanes and rammed into me suddenly and it was a couple on a Splendor or something. Before I could pick my tank bag and my bike and settle down, they got up, they were in shock too but they went away on their motorcycle. I was blank and it didn't occur for me to note down their registration number or get their details. And my Speed 400 wouldn't start. Gear lever was bent, whole front end was disorientated. I called Triumph support and I waited for 4 hrs while the recovery van from the RSA I got arrived. They loaded the motorcycle and said they'll take it to the nearest Triumph showroom which for me was Retro Triumph in Banjara Hills, Hyderabad. After giving the RSA guy the keys, I went home and dealt with the service manager via phone as I was living in a different city.

2.) Even though the first party insurance I had was from the Triumph dealership in Vijayawada, Andhra Pradesh (where I took the delivery) there wasn't a cashless tie up with my insurance company (UIIC) and the Triumph SC in Hyderabad. I had to pay 60k and later the insurance company reimbursed 46k out of it. I was a little surprised as I also had zero dep but that's what I received.

3.) I had to renew my first party this August and I did it myself after enquiring which of the Triumph SCs had cashless tie ups with which companies in TG and AP. I went with ICICI lombard as it has cashless tie up with most of the SCs in AP and TG (as I travel between these states the most). It costed me close to 6k with return to invoice, zero dep, RSA, consumables and engine protect add ons. I would say more than just getting the first party renewed from the dealership, if you travel like me between 2 states, make sure to enquire which insurance company has cashless tie ups with the majority of the SCs so that in case of an unfortunate incident like a crash, you have better settlement experience. Even if you just live in one city, you can renew the insurance yourself for a lower price, just enquire which insurance companies the service centre has cashless tie ups with. It could even be the same company you're with right now. I did the same for car insurance this year but Maruti Suzuki wasn't happy about me renewing it myself. A representative of theirs called and spoke in a very threatening manner saying I would not have a smooth experience as I didn't get it renewed by them. I asked why and how it is different, he didn't have an answer but said the same thing again that it would just be a smoother process in a case I had to claim. The irony is I went for the same company I had last year, but I was getting it for a lower price if I did it myself rather than get it done through Maruti Suzuki as a broker. So yeah wanted to share that as well. 

Happy riding and good to see you have the Classic 350 back Amit! 😃
